methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Ground Control Development is a seed-stage housing and construction company founded by Lizzy Manzi that has raised $2M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of five private peers in the frontier construction-tech space—BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Unlimited Industries, ADMARES, and Hedral—given the absence of directly comparable public companies in this subsector.

The stage-progression method was the applicable triangulation technique. Using total capital raised ($2M) as a proxy for seed-stage value and applying a 2.5x multiplier to reflect typical step-up dynamics from Seed to the next institutional round, this method implies a valuation of $5M. This represents the median and only quantitative anchor in the analysis.

The triangulated valuation range is $4M (low) to $6M (high), with a $5M median. Key uncertainties reflect the constraint of a single applicable method and the limited public data on private peer valuations. Relative positioning within the comp set, burn trajectory, and customer traction would be material inputs to confidence in this range. The analysis should be revisited as the company approaches its Series A and private peer data becomes more granular.
